text:
Avery: Thanks for joining the post-all-hands Q&A thread. Drop any quick clarifying questions about strategy, messaging, market focus, or competitor calls and well answer inline.
Liam: Two-part Q: 1) should we frame Redwood as primarily a performance play or a platform play in customer decks? 2) any embargoed competitive intel we need to watch?
Maya: Short take for 1) lead with performance & economics to get engineering attention, then show platform breadth for procurement/stakeholders. For 2) nothing new public; follow legal on sensitive comparisons.
Ravi: For product folks: what roadmap signals are safe to mention publicly? e.g., "improved KV caching coming Q3" vs broad claims like "lowest latency"
Ellen: Use milestone phrasing: "upcoming KV-caching optimizations (H2)" is fine. Avoid absolutes like "lowest" unless you can cite a benchmark.
Sofia: Sales asked whether we should proactively compare against TopCloud in RFPs on latency. Any dos/don'ts?
Maya: Do: present head-to-head metrics when you have reproducible suites. Don't: cherry-pick tests that customers will replicate and find different results. Offer to run joint benchmarks for high-intent buyers.
Liam: Is the phrase "model-agnostic serving" approved for marketing? want to include in AE pitch.
Avery: Approved. Use exact copy: "Model-agnostic serving with Redwood-verified performance profiles." That balances neutrality and trust.
Ravi: Are we updating the positioning statement on the website or just marketing assets?
Avery: Both. Marketing will push a refreshed headline and AE kits; web updates will follow next week.
Ellen: Question from support: when customers ask "why not just use managed endpoints from cloudX?", what's our succinct reply?
Maya: "Managed cloud endpoints are convenient; Redwood focuses on predictable latency, lower unit cost at scale, and operational controls suited for production LLM workloads." Keep it 1-2 lines.
Sofia: Competitors to call out in sales playbooks? need a short list.
BenchmarkBot: Common comparatives: BigCloud managed endpoints, ModelCo self-hosted stacks, FastServe runtimes.
Liam: Any change to our go-to-market segmentation? who is the highest priority: AI-native startups or enterprise platform teams?
Avery: Continue PLG-first motion to capture AI-native growth; accelerate targeted motions for platform/enterprise accounts where Dedicated/Private fit. Both matter, but different motions.
Ravi: Budgeting question for product: will we prioritize latency optimizations (kernel work) or features like structured outputs this quarter?
Maya: Split effort: focus engineering sprints on low-hanging latency wins plus one feature sprint for structured outputs. Well publish a short roadmap note.
Ellen: Request: can leadership drop a one-paragraph summary here for AEs to copy into deal emails?
Avery: Will post a short, copy-ready paragraph by EOD today.
Sofia: Thanks 44f3fb. Also, can someone link the perf benchmark repo for AEs to reference?
BenchmarkBot: Perf repo: https://git.example.com/redwood/perf-suites. Use the "public-ae-quick" branch for sanitized numbers.
Avery: Great thread. Keep questions coming. If anyone needs a deeper sync, ping me or book time on my calendar. :calendar:
